newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 18.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Tyco International and ADT announce $5.4 billion merger, topping a hostile takeover offer by Western Resources Inc.
* H.F. Ahmanson sweetens a hostile tender offer for Great Western to $6.68 billion.
* Rockwell announced plans to spin-off its automotive business, in its transformation to a company more focused on electronics.
* An administration plan to revamp the Internal Revenue Service is trying to block more radical Congressional proposals to change the agency.
* Advanta said it expected to post a net loss in the first quarter due to loan losses and a revenue slump. It also said it was looking at alternatives, including a sale of the company.
* Northwest Air may have ordered about 40 Airbus A-330, paying as much as $4.2 billion, sources familiar with the deal said.
* Ford said it would start making prototypes of efficient cars later this year.
* Flagstar FLGS.O agreed in principle to recapitalize under a plan which would give creditors about 95.5 percent of the company.
* The Justice Department has asked Raytheon for more information, which could delay its proposed acquisition of Texas Instruments.
* News Corp is in discussions over buying PointCast, an Internet broadcaster. It also agreed to buy Heritage Media for $754 million.
* The Supreme Court declined to hear a challenge to a Florida law permitting the state to sue cigarette makers for the cost of smoking-related illnesses.
* The Dow Jones industrials recovered from a 81-point drop to end up 20.02 at 6955.48.
* Salomon said it would restate its fourth quarter as a loss because it agreed to sell Basis Petroleum to Valero Energy.
* The NASD and the Nasdaq National Stock Market formed a task force to pass on to authorities leads about potential organized crime involvement in U.S. stock markets.

* Heard on the Street: ITT's Harold Geneen, American Express' James Robinson III and Martin Davis, the 67-year-old former chairman of what is now Viacom's Paramount Communications. They've all busied themselves in recent years with small companies after departing from the bright lights and the high-stakes business of ruling a multi-billion dollar corporate empire.

* Credit markets: Although most stock and bond markets shrugged off the Federal Reserve Chairman's Feb 26 warning about risk in both the stock and bond markets, bonds from developing countries known as emerging markets have fallen sharply in the past 2-1/2 weeks.
